domain.basis: Read the complete frozen report, lines 1-294, its research question and effective requirements. Domain: on-device inference, hardware memory and edge-cloud system design. Qwen official complete config gives 36 layers, 2 KV heads, head dimension 128 and disabled sliding window: BF16 batch-one cache is 36 KiB/token, 144/288/1152 MiB at 4K/8K/32K. The 4 GiB available-memory budget, artifact overheads and index reservation are explicitly scenarios, not Android entitlements; memory calculations do not borrow Gemma throughput. Quantization discussion preserves weight/activation/KV differences, Meta quality rows and Apple July-2025 compression Table 3; original table images checked. Historical LiteRT rows really belong to S24 Ultra at the pinned July-2025 commit, with correct rates and 1024/256 tokens, but the known Android performance-lock condition is omitted (finding). BaseRT original experimental setup and Tables 1-3 support the M4 Pro 16-core/24GB/273GB/s configuration, runtime baselines and separate phase arithmetic; report does not promote it to combined end-to-end measurement. MELT sustained iPhone/Jetson findings are kept historical, not transferred to S24. Minions final ICML Table 1 image and Table 2 text support .724/.709, $.233/$.042 and 31.81 vs 11 s on RTX4090; local-free accounting, workstation latency and privacy limits remain explicit. WhisperTRT pinned README, complete profiling code, live VAD/ASR process and transcribe implementation support warm single-clip timings, RSS delta rather than peak, MiB label correction, greedy decoder, utterance-end processing and 30-second truncation. ASR paper setup pp4-7 and visual Table4 p10 support the 70 short clips, synthetic noise procedure, baseline-subtracted CPU/GPU energy and FP16/INT8 tradeoff; these are not wall energy or the WhisperTRT experiment. Existing complete calculation code and retained results match memory, latency, duty-power, transfer and cost tables; no model or calculation rerun. Economic denominators consistently separate incoming from accepted tasks and existing from dedicated hardware. Current platform evidence supports Phi/LAF/China/Insider-transition limits, ML Kit foreground/quota limitations, PCC entitlement/context distinction and QNN static quantized graphs; privacy discussion separates local execution, remote content, logging and training/retention. Whole-report deployment recommendations remain conditional on task quality, readiness and sustained measurements, with the single experimental-condition correction below.

findings.basis: The pinned LiteRT-LM README eaa380eee74b677f9f305eb2a92ae0fcc14ffc39 explicitly states at lines 62-64 that the 1024-token prefill / 256-token decode benchmarks use performance lock on Android devices. The report preserves model, backend, context and rates but omits this known operating condition, including where it projects 9.46 s and 34.07 s for interactive use. A locked-performance benchmark has a different operating constraint from ordinary governor-managed mobile use; the existing statement that thermal history is unreported does not disclose the lock. This matters to the requested hardware/runtime/power envelope and transferability of the phone timing. Add the source-stated performance-lock condition beside the initial S24 measurements and carry it with the interpretation of derived times. Do not invent a lock implementation, power draw or slowdown: these are not supplied by the source. The table arithmetic and historical device attribution themselves are correct.
